stories.title: Researchers address 'Sequential Distraction' in omni-modal GUI agents
stories.summary: A new paper identifies 'Sequential Distraction' in GUI agents that process streaming omni-modal observations, where context useful for one action becomes clutter the next and errors compound.
stories.more: GUI agents that act on streaming screenshots, audio, video, and device states can be misled when context stays relevant only briefly before becoming noise. The paper argues that because executed actions feed back into context, these errors compound over time into what it calls Sequential Distraction, pushing agents toward irreversible mistakes. The excerpt does not detail the proposed fix or benchmark results.

stories.title: PAR method aims to fix length generalization in looped language models
stories.summary: A new technique called Progress-Aligned Recurrence trains looped language models to match their internal state after each reasoning step, aiming to fix poor length generalization in state tracking.
stories.more: Looped language models can run extra iterations at test time, but the paper notes this doesn't reliably help them solve longer problems, since final-answer supervision doesn't specify how far each iteration should advance. PAR trains the prediction at each iteration to match the state after that many operations, and rescales the recurrent state relative to its first iteration. The excerpt does not include evaluation results.

items.title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
items.excerpt: Looped language models can run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems. For sequential state tracking, final-answer supervision does not specify how far each iteration should advance, and repeated updates can change the scale of the recurrent state. stories.title: VPM world model forecasts multi-view video and 3D point trajectories
stories.summary: A new world model called VPM conditions on multi-view video history and language instructions to jointly forecast future video and the 3D paths of scene points.
stories.more: VPM extends a pretrained world model with camera-conditioned multi-view processing, integrating observations across multiple cameras to keep forecasts of the same evolving 3D scene consistent. It jointly predicts future video from arbitrary viewpoints alongside the 3D trajectories of persistent points in the scene. The excerpt does not specify training data, benchmarks, or results.

stories.title: SolarRenderer turns coarse scene structure into video in few steps
stories.summary: SolarRenderer is a structure-conditioned video renderer that turns coarse layout, motion, and camera specs from game engines or coding agents into realistic video in fewer denoising steps.
stories.more: The paper says existing renderers are tied to one engine's representation, need many denoising steps or costly distillation, and are trained on conditions misaligned with their target videos. SolarRenderer is designed to follow input structure while filling in the appearance it leaves open, in few generative steps. The excerpt does not give step counts, benchmarks, or comparisons to specific existing renderers.

Existing renderers are tied to the representation of one engine, need tens of denoising steps or a costly distillation of their own, and learn from conditions that are not aligned with their target videos. stories.title: VLA-Rolling reuses discarded action predictions to cut denoising steps
stories.summary: VLA-Rolling shows that the unexecuted 'action tail' flow-matching robot policies normally discard still carries useful denoising progress, letting replanning match or beat a native 10-step baseline.
stories.more: Flow-matching vision-language-action models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising noise but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with new observations, discarding the rest. The paper finds this discarded tail retains transferable denoising progress, so initializing the next chunk from it can match or outperform a native 10-step Gaussian baseline. The excerpt does not specify exact step savings or which robot tasks were tested.

items.title: VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
items.excerpt: Flow-matching vision-language-action (VLA) models generate an action chunk by iteratively denoising Gaussian noise, but typically execute only a short prefix before replanning with updated observations. Under this receding-horizon paradigm, the unexecuted remainder---the action tail---is discarded, and the next chunk is regenerated from fresh noise. stories.title: SWIFT uses a frozen weak model to sharpen diffusion training for free
stories.summary: SWIFT is a self-guided training method that uses a frozen weak denoiser to improve a stronger diffusion model's quality without adding cost at inference time.
stories.more: Training high-quality diffusion models is expensive, and guiding them at inference time usually adds further sampling cost. SWIFT instead extrapolates the clean regression target away from a frozen weak denoiser's prediction for each noisy input, amplifying the components the stronger model still underfits. The weak guide can be an early checkpoint of the same model. The excerpt does not report specific quality gains or benchmark comparisons.

stories.title: Private keys for eight eMudhra root-chained CA certificates compromised
stories.summary: Simon Willison flags the compromise of private keys for eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authority certificates, which chain to roots trusted by major browsers and operating systems.
stories.more: The compromised certificates chain to roots trusted by Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple, and Chrome's root programs, and by many downstream trust stores, meaning any software bundling a trusted-certificate list needs updating, including Linux distributions' ca-certificates packages. Willison links to a GitHub repository tracking which software has issued updates in response, and notes the Python package manager uv was affected. The excerpt does not say how the keys were compromised or which certificate authority disclosed the breach.

items.title: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise
items.excerpt: eMudhra Intermediate CA Compromise This is very, very bad news: The private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates have been compromised. They chain to roots trusted by the Mozilla, Microsoft, Apple and Chrome root programs and by many downstream trust stores. Any software that bundles a list of trusted certificates needs to be updated. This site is tracking software updates via this GitHub repository - Linux distros need to update their ca-certificates packages. In Python world uv 0
